In this lesson you will learn about the bistable multivibrator.
INTRODUCTIONM
Bistable multivibrators change the DC operating voltage to a square wave output.
The bistable multivibrator is triggered. It has two stable states.
The components in the feedback circuit determine the bistable operation.

BISTABLE MULTIVIBRATOR
This is a typical bistable multivibrator circuit...........
DISCUSSION
It is identified as a bistable multivibrator by the feedback circuit containing R2, C2 and R3, C3.
The circuit consists of two common emitter amplifiers. Notice that NPN transistors are used.
Q1 amplifier uses R1, R3,R4 and R5 for biasing.
R1 is the collector load resistor. R3 and R5 are voltage divider base bias resistors. The base bias voltage is taken between R5 and R3.
Q2 amplifier uses R4, R2, R6 and R1 for biasing.
R4 is the collector load resistor. R2 and R6 are voltage divider base bias resistors. The base bias voltage is taken between R6 and R2.
R2, C2 and R3, C3 cross couple the output of one amplifier to the input of the other amplifier.
C2 and C3 are speed up capacitors. They immediately couple a change in voltage from the collector of one transistor to the base of the other transistor.
C1, D1 and C4, D2 are used to input the trigger pulse. A negative input is required to forward bias the diodes.
R7 and R8 apply a bias to D1 and D2 so that only one diode is forward biased for each stable state of the multivibrator.

FIRST STATE OF THE MULTIVIBRATOR
Q1 ON, 0 V on collector: Q1 turns on because it started to conduct first.
FIRST STATE OF THE MULTIVIBRATOR

Q2 OFF, +12V on collector: Q2 turns off because of the zero voltage on the collector of Q1...............
The circuit stays in this state until an input trigger is received.
With Q1 ON, 0 V is applied to the cathode of D1, it is forward biased. With Q2 OFF, +12V is applied to the cathode of D2, it is reverse biased.
When the negative input pulse is received, D1 allows the pulse to pass to the base of Q1. D2 blocks the path to the base of Q2.
The negative pulse on the base of Q1 turns it OFF. The collector voltage raises to +12V.
At the instant Q1 turns OFF, C2 couples the raise in collector voltage to the base of Q2.
The positive voltage on the base of Q2 turns it ON. The collector voltage decreases to 0V.
The 0V on the collector of Q2 is applied by the voltage divider of R3 and R5, to the base of Q1. Q1 remains OFF.
SECOND STATE OF THE MULTIVIBRATOR
Q1 OFF, +12V on collector: Q1 was turned OFF by the negative input pulse.
SECOND STATE OF THE MULTIVIBRATOR
Q1 OFF, +12V on collector: Q1 was turned OFF by the negative input pulse.
Q2 ON, 0V on collector: Q2 was turned ON by the +12V on the collector of Q1.
With Q1 OFF, +12 V is applied to the cathode of D1, it is reverse biased. With Q2 ON, 0V is applied to the cathode of D2, it is forward biased.
When a negative input pulse is received, D2 allows the pulse to pass to the base of Q2. D1 blocks the path to the base of Q1.
The negative pulse on the base of Q2 turns it OFF. The collector voltage raises to +12 V.
At the instant Q2 turns OFF, C3 couples the raise in collector voltage to the base of Q1.
The positive voltage on the base of Q1 turns it ON. The collector voltage decreases to 0V.
The 0 V on the collector of Q1 is applied to the base of Q2. Q2 remains OFF.
RETURN TO THE FIRST STABLE STATE
Q1 ON, 0V on collector: Q1 turned ON by the +V on the collector of Q2.
RETURN TO THE FIRST STABLE STATE
Q1 ON, 0V on collector: Q1 turns on by the +V on the collector of Q2.
Q2 OFF, +12V on collector: Q2 turned OFF by the negative input pulse.
Remember, when the trigger pulse is received, only one diode is forward biased.
The forward biased diode connects the negative input pulse to the base of the transistor that is ON.
The negative trigger pulse turns Q1 OFF, this turns Q2 ON./

Normal operation of a bistable multivibrator is checked by measuring the output frequency with an oscilloscope or frequency counter.
Then compare the measured output frequency with one half of the frequency of the trigger pulses.
The output frequency is one half of the trigger frequency because of the two stable states of the multivibrator.
If the first trigger pulse turns Q1 OFF and Q2 ON, the output is 0 V, half a cycle.
The second trigger pulse turns Q2 OFF and Q1 ON, the output is +12V, the second half cycle.
It takes two trigger pulses to produce one output cycle.
For example, the output frequency of this bistable multivibrator is 2.5 kHz.
